proposals.before: Early in the Tiancheng era his son Fa disinterred it and took it away.
proposals.after: Early in the Tiancheng era his son disinterred it and took it away.
proposals.reason: Chinese 其子發之攜去 means the son dug it up (發之) and carried it away; 發 is the verb, not a personal name Fa.

proposals.before: At the beginning of the Tiancheng reign his son Fa took it away.
proposals.after: At the beginning of the Tiancheng reign his son dug it up and took it away.
proposals.reason: Literal English invents the name Fa; 發之 means opened/disinterred it.

proposals.before: Li declared himself acting commissioner and led soldiers and civilians in a memorial requesting formal appointment.
proposals.after: Yang Li declared himself acting commissioner and led soldiers and civilians in a memorial requesting formal appointment.
proposals.reason: Subject is 立 (Yang Li); rendering as Li wrongly suggests a different Li-surname figure.

proposals.before: Zhuangzong was furious and ordered Mingzong and Li Shaozhen to attack. Within a month the city fell. Li and more than ten of his accomplices were taken alive, sent to the capital, and dismembered in the marketplace.
proposals.after: Zhuangzong was furious and ordered Mingzong and Li Shaozhen to attack. Within a month the city fell. Yang Li and more than ten of his accomplices were taken alive, sent to the capital, and dismembered in the marketplace.
proposals.reason: Second Li refers to Yang Li (立), not another Li; needs disambiguation from Li Shaozhen in the same sentence.

proposals.before: Luzhou's walls were high and its moat deep, yet Li had dared to hold it. Zhuangzong therefore ordered every circuit to dismantle its outer defensive works.
proposals.after: Luzhou's walls were high and its moat deep, yet Yang Li had dared to hold it. Zhuangzong therefore ordered every circuit to dismantle its outer defensive works.
proposals.reason: Referent is Yang Li (立), not an unspecified Li.

proposals.before: Before long Chongtao was killed on Siji's orders. The two men then turned on Dong Zhang. "Which door will you straddle now?" they demanded."
proposals.after: Before long Chongtao was killed on Siji's orders. The two men then turned on Dong Zhang. "Which door will you straddle now?" they demanded.
proposals.reason: Extraneous closing quotation mark after demanded.

decisions.reason: 其子發之攜去: 發之 is the verb phrase “disinterred/opened it,” not a personal name; inventing “Fa” as the son’s name is unsupported, and removing it restores the Chinese.
Literal English invents “Fa”; 發之 must be rendered as dug up/disinterred, and 攜去 as took it away—the proposed literal matches the Chinese.
Subject 立 is Yang Li’s given name; bare “Li” in English reads as a Li-surname agent and conflicts with nearby 李繼珂. Expanding to Yang Li correctly identifies the referent.
生擒立 is Yang Li (立), while 李紹真 is a different Li; bare “Li” after naming Li Shaozhen misattributes the captive. “Yang Li” disambiguates correctly.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 生擒立及其同惡十餘人

decisions.reason: 攻立輒敢據之 continues the Yang Li (立) rebellion narrative; English “Li” is ambiguous and should be Yang Li.
Chinese closes the dialogue at 何門？; the idiomatic already ends the quote at “now?”, so the extra closing quote after “demanded.” is a punctuation error with no source support.
